info.title: Commerce Connector API
info.description: The Commerce Connector API provides endpoints to manage data exchanges, configure transmission settings, monitor processing logs, and integrate with external systems via SFTP, HTTPS, and Azure Blob Storage.

get.description:
Retrieves a list of available commerce connectors that can be used as native data exchanges. Each connector includes attributes such as Exchange Name, Exchange Code, Version, Tags, Library, Collection, Data Source, and Access.

---

### Filter Support

**Filter Format:** `filter={Field}~{Operator}~{Value}`

**Supported Filter Fields & Operators:**

| Field | Supported Operators |
|-------|---------------------|
| Name | cn (Contains), ew (EndsWith), sw (StartsWith), lk (Like), is (Is), or (OR), ncn (NotContains), nlk (NotLike) |
| ExchangeCode | cn (Contains), ew (EndsWith), sw (StartsWith), lk (Like), is (Is), or (OR), ncn (NotContains), nlk (NotLike) |
| Tags | cn (Contains), ew (EndsWith), sw (StartsWith), lk (Like), is (Is), or (OR), ncn (NotContains), nlk (NotLike) |

**Example:**
- `filter=Name~cn~Customer`
- `filter=Tags~is~Import`

For the full list of operators and usage, see [Filters, Pagination & Sorting](https://apidocs.znode.com/docs/data-exchanges/branches/main/lmod0vga5s303).

---

### Sort Support

**Sort Format:** `sort={Field}~{asc|desc}`

**Supported Sort Fields:**

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Name | Sort by the data exchange name. |
| ExchangeCode | Sort by the unique exchange code. |

---

### Pagination

Supports `pageIndex` and `pageSize` parameters. See [Filters, Pagination & Sorting](https://apidocs.znode.com/docs/data-exchanges/branches/main/lmod0vga5s303) for details.

---

### Related APIs

- **`GET`** [Retrieve all data exchanges.](https://apidocs.znode.com/docs/data-exchanges/branches/main/0feb27zyg2wh7)

post.summary: Create a data exchange from the native library
post.description:
Adds a selected native data exchange library entry to the data exchange list. If added successfully, returns a boolean response.

If no data exchange is selected when the user clicks Add, the system returns a validation error prompting the user to select a data exchange.

If the selected data exchange already exists in the list, the user must provide a new exchange code and exchange name. A new entry will be created using the new code and name while copying all configuration and data from the selected data exchange ID.

post.summary: Process the configured source API and retrieve data
post.description:
Retrieves source data by invoking the Commerce Connector's Input Handler to call the configured source endpoint. The connector supports multiple transmission methods, including **API**, **SFTP**, and **BLOB**, allowing data to be retrieved from a variety of external systems and storage locations. The retrieved data is processed according to the YAML configuration defined for the connector and can be used with custom processors to support specialized data transformation and processing workflows.

Supported transmission methods include:

- **API** – Retrieves data from an external application using a configured API endpoint.
- **SFTP** – Retrieves data files from a configured SFTP server.
- **BLOB** – Retrieves data from a configured blob storage location.

For **API-based integrations**, the connector supports the following authentication methods:

- **Basic Authentication** – Authenticates requests using an API Key, Username, Password, or a combination of these credentials.
- **OAuth 2.0 Authentication** – Supports industry-standard OAuth 2.0 authorization flows for secure, token-based access to protected APIs.

For a given exchange code and log ID, the API accepts a single log message per request. When a new request is received, the existing log message is retrieved and the new message is appended to it. Therefore, if multiple messages need to be recorded for the same process log, each message must be submitted through a separate API request.

---

### Recording the final job status from a custom processor

When a custom processor does not use the standard Znode handlers, the processor must call this API to record the final result of the job.

When a data exchange runs a custom processor, Znode creates a process log entry with the status **Started** and then calls the `execute-data-exchange` endpoint of the Custom API. Znode does not update that log entry again when the custom processor finishes, so this API must be called as the last step of every run.

If this API is not called, the processing can finish successfully while **Dev Center > Commerce Connector > Data Exchange Logs** in the Znode Admin continues to show the job as **Started** or **Failed**, with no end date.

**Where the log ID comes from**

Znode passes the log ID of the current run to the custom processor as the `logId` query parameter when it starts the run:

`GET {CustomApiUrl}/CustomDataExchange/custom-data-exchange/execute-data-exchange?erpId={erpId}&logId={logId}`

Use this `logId` in this API, together with the exchange code of the same data exchange. Each run has its own log ID, so do not reuse a log ID from an earlier run. If the exchange code does not own the log ID, the API returns `404 Not Found`.

**When to call it**

Call this API after all custom processing for the run is complete, whether the run succeeded or failed. Every call sets the status, the record counts and the end date of the log, and the last call made is what the Admin shows. Calling it before processing is complete marks the job as finished too early.

**What to send**

| Outcome | `status` | `successRecordCount` / `failedRecordCount` | `logMessage` / `logType` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run succeeded | `true` (shown as **Completed Successfully**) | Final counts for the whole run | Completion message, `Info` |
| Run failed | `false` (shown as **Failed**) | Counts processed before the failure | Reason for the failure, `Error` |

- Always send `status`. If it is omitted, the job is recorded as **Failed**.
- The record counts are final totals for the run. They replace the counts on the log and are not added to them. Total processed records is the sum of the two counts.
- The end date of the log is set to the time of the call.

Example of a successful run:

```json
{
  "successRecordCount": 1250,
  "failedRecordCount": 3,
  "status": true,
  "logMessage": "Facebook feed generated: 1250 products exported, 3 skipped.",
  "logType": "Info"
}
```

Example of a failed run:

```json
{
  "successRecordCount": 0,
  "failedRecordCount": 0,
  "status": false,
  "logMessage": "Feed upload failed: destination server refused the connection.",
  "logType": "Error"
}
```

**Long-running jobs**

Znode waits for `execute-data-exchange` to return. If it returns `false`, returns an error or times out, Znode records the job as **Failed**, even if the processing is still running. For long-running jobs, return from `execute-data-exchange` once processing has started, run the work in the background, and call this API when the work is complete. The status sent to this API replaces the status recorded by Znode.

IsSuccess.description: Returns `true` if the operation completed successfully; `false` otherwise.

ErrorMessage.description: A human-readable error message returned when the operation fails.

HasError.description: Returns `true` if an error occurred; `false` if the operation completed successfully.

SuccessMessage.description: A confirmation message returned when the operation completes successfully.

successRecordCount.description: Number of successful records processed. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

failedRecordCount.description: Number of failed records processed. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

status.description: Indicates the processing status for the data exchange. If status is true, the message set will be Completed Successfully; in case of status false, the message set is Failed.

logMessage.description: Detailed log message describing the process output or error details. The API accepts a single log message per request and appends it to any existing log message for the specified process log. LogMessage and LogType must be provided together. Both fields are required when one is specified.
logMessage.example: Data exchange process completed with 100 successful records and 2 failed records.

logType.description: Specifies the process log trace level. Allowed values: Off, Error, Warning, Info, Verbose. LogMessage and LogType must be provided together. Both fields are required when one is specified.
